editorial.headline: The Retail Trade Behind Pharmaceutical Inputs and Health Devices
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans specialist retail in pharmaceutical ingredients, traditional-medicine raw materials, health devices and animal-health outlets—with a clear national and Bali PMA position.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47729 concerns the retail trade in specialist goods that sit behind health care and animal care. Its scope includes pharmaceutical-preparation ingredients and traditional-medicine raw materials—*simplisia*—for both people and animals, as well as other health devices. It also encompasses veterinary pharmacies, animal-medicine depots, pet shops, poultry shops and animal-medicine stores. The unifying idea is retail: businesses sell these inputs, devices and animal-health goods to the market rather than producing them.

The activity is open across every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the code describes a retail field with room for different operating models, from smaller specialist shops to larger businesses handling a wider commercial range. The record does not divide these activities into separate regulatory stories; it presents them together as one retail activity whose character is defined by its goods and outlets.

Nationally, the PMA status is open, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. For a foreign-investment business, that is the central national position: the activity is not presented as subject to a foreign-equity cap below full ownership. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali requires a more precise reading, but not a pessimistic one. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This record is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its stated reason is that, at the Large scale, OSS risk is Medium-High/High, placing it outside that moratorium’s blocking criterion. The Bali status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a business should read the national openness and the Bali result together, with the applicable scale and its stated risk position at the centre of the assessment.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this activity is not marked as blocked for PMA in Bali because its Large-scale OSS risk sits above the moratorium’s blocking threshold.
